slot.brief: Given standard potentials of two couples involving a common metal, compute E° of the cell formed by combining them.

stem: The standard reduction potentials are $E^\circ_{\text{Fe}^{3+}/\text{Fe}^{2+}}=+0.77$ V and $E^\circ_{\text{Fe}^{2+}/\text{Fe}}=-0.44$ V. What is the standard EMF when these half-cells are combined?

verdicts.working: The Fe³⁺/Fe²⁺ half-cell is the cathode and Fe/Fe²⁺ is the anode. E°cell = 0.77 − (−0.44) = 1.21 V.

working:
Cathode: $\text{Fe}^{3+}+e^-\rightarrow\text{Fe}^{2+}$; anode: $\text{Fe}\rightarrow\text{Fe}^{2+}+2e^-$. 
$E^\circ_{\text{cell}}=E^\circ_{\text{cathode}}-E^\circ_{\text{anode, reduction}}$
$=0.77-(-0.44)=1.21\ \text{V}$.

Independent check: The Fe³⁺/Fe²⁺ half-cell is the cathode and Fe/Fe²⁺ is the anode. E°cell = 0.77 − (−0.44) = 1.21 V.
solution:
The Fe$^{3+}$/Fe$^{2+}$ half-cell is the cathode, and Fe/Fe$^{2+}$ is the anode.
$$E^\firc_{\text{cell}}=E^\firc_{\text{cathode}}-E^\firc_{\text{anode, reduction}}=0.77-(-0.44)=1.21\text{ V}$$

draft.distractor_notes: A: Treats the iron oxidation potential as $+0.44$ V. B: Uses only the cathode potential. D: Adds the potentials without changing the sign of the anode reduction potential.
